correctness.rationale: The actual smooth witness h_eps=1+eps[(u1^2-1/d)+(u1^3-3u1/(d+2))] defines a strictly convex support for sufficiently small nonzero eps by positivity of its spherical Hessian-plus-metric tensor. The first spherical moment vanishes; exact E[u1^2],E[u1^4],E[u1^6] yield E[u1(H2+H3)^2]=12(d-1)/[d(d+2)^2(d+4)], independently reconstructed from the mixed harmonic moment. For each ball radius R the optimization over all Euclidean isometries reduces to translation, and the Lp power is coercive and strictly convex in x, so its minimizer is unique. Expanding the exact first-order Euler condition with delta=1/R, the implicit-function derivative is x'(0)=-d(p-2)/2 times the squared-support first moment; the displayed drift follows and is nonzero at all sufficiently large finite R while tending to zero. Equivariance forces s(RB+x_R)=x_R, so association would force the fixed body s(X_eps) to equal all these varying centers, contradiction. The p=2 leading coefficient vanishes; finite p>2 and d>=2 essential.

value.rationale: Provides a complete negative answer to an explicit 2009 open problem for every finite p>2 and d>=2, not a contrived example. The explicit (p-2)/R drift reveals exactly why the obstruction disappears at the Hilbert exponent and shows a geometric distinction between support-metric optimization and centroid-based equivariance.

final_claim: For every Euclidean dimension d>=2 and finite p>2, no Euclidean-isometry-equivariant point selector on full-dimensional compact convex bodies can be associated with the Lp spherical support-function distance; a smooth strictly convex witness has a nonzero p-dependent optimal large-ball center drift x_R=-6(p-2)(d-1)eps^2/[(d+2)^2(d+4)R] e1+O(R^-2).
limitations: For finite 2<p<infinity and d>=2 on nonempty-interior convex bodies; original Hausdorff p=infinity and Hilbert p=2 results are not new.
Large-R expansion does not quantify the full finite-R optimal centers.
